candidate_lesson.lesson_text: When the 30-indicator consensus shows dir=LONG at conv=100% but green_matches ≤ 1, the historical hit rate is unreliable (small-sample) and the signal should be sized down or gated until green_matches ≥ 3.
candidate_lesson.mechanism: green_matches counts how many times a similar live indicator configuration recurred in the historical memory bank. A conv=100% reading with green_matches=1 (EURUSD hist_hr=73%) rests on a single analog — that 73% is an artifact of one lucky path, not a stable base rate. Institutional flow that produces durable directional edges leaves repeated footprints; a one-off configuration is more likely regime-noise than a reproducible setup, so trusting the printed hist_hr overstates true expectancy.
candidate_lesson.testable_rule: if consensus.dir in ('LONG','SHORT') and consensus.conv >= 0.99 and consensus.green_matches <= 1: size_multiplier *= 0.5  # compare realized R vs green_matches >= 3 cohort
candidate_lesson.expected_impact: Reduces variance drag from thin-analog entries; expected Sharpe +0.02–0.04 by suppressing low-confidence high-conviction traps (EURUSD-type green_matches=1 signals) without cutting the green_matches=5 GBPUSD cohort.
candidate_lesson.evidence_from_harvest: Live consensus shows GBPUSD (green_matches=5, hist_hr=68%) and AUDUSD (green_matches=3, hist_hr=68%) as well-supported LONGs, while EURUSD prints identical conv=100% but green_matches=1 hist_hr=73% — an inflated rate on a single analog. USDJPY/AUDNZD with green_matches=0 correctly show hist_hr=0%, confirming green_matches is the reliability axis, not conviction.
